definitions.title: Set-piece definition
definitions.body: A set piece is a corner, a free kick, or a long throw from the attacking third into the box or covering at least 20 m. Penalties are excluded from set-piece metrics and reported separately. Phase one is the first 5 seconds after delivery or at most one extra pass; the total window is 20 seconds. Coordinates are on a 105 × 68 m pitch with the attacked goal at x = 105.

sources.title: Data sources
sources.body: League tables and team statistics come from the seed file (seed:super_lig.json) and every number shows its source. No web scraping is used; only licensed providers, StatsBomb Open Data (for development and validation) and files the club imports itself.

statsbomb.title: StatsBomb Open Data
statsbomb.body: Set-piece extraction was validated against StatsBomb Open Data event data. The data is used under StatsBomb's open data licence and attribution terms and is not committed to the repository. Data: StatsBomb.

imports.title: Imported data
imports.body: Files uploaded by the club go through quality checks. A file with critical issues is quarantined and never reaches the metrics. Committed data is visible only to the uploading club and its source is shown as "import".

limits.title: Limitations
limits.body: Rates and counts are shrunk for small samples; fewer than 8 attempts or 5 matches shows a "Small sample" badge. Aerials, fouls and clearances are indirect indicators for defending and are labelled as such.

scatter.title: Set-piece xG and goals
scatter.description: Each dot is a team; horizontal axis set-piece xG, vertical axis set-piece goals. Dashed line is goals = xG.
scatter.caption: Teams above the dashed line scored more than their xG; the gap is not a persistent skill signal. The amber dot is your club.
